item.title: Trump Bars Some South Africans Over Claims of Anti-White Discrimination
item.description: Washington says South Africa has not done anything to fix what President Trump sees as discrimination. South Africa’s president has called Mr. Trump’s policies racist.
item.dc:creator: John Eligon
item.media:description: President Trump and President Cyril Ramaphosa of South Africa meeting in the Oval Office in Washington last year.

item.title: The Subtle Sign That A.I. Is Not Yet a National Political Issue
item.description: A Times/Siena poll shows many voters are still uncertain on the issue, including which party would do a better job on it.

item.title: The World Economy Is Becoming Wary of the U.S.
item.description: America’s position of global economic stability is starting to look shakier as the Trump administration piles on debt and doubles down on sanctions.
item.dc:creator: Alan Rappeport

item.title: ‘You’re Elected to Fight and Kill the Other Side’: How Congress Lost Its Way
item.description: Members from both parties say the legislative branch has descended into a state of dysfunction in the Trump era.
item.dc:creator: Robert Draper

item.title: Trump Plans Blitz of $138 Million and Counting to Save Midterm Republicans
item.description: His powerful super PAC is suddenly spending heavily on some races, after drawing fire from some Republicans that the group might not throw its weight behind the party’s candidates.
item.dc:creator: Theodore Schleifer, Shane Goldmacher and Maggie Haberman
item.media:description: President Trump’s super PAC, MAGA Inc., has amassed more than $400 million.

item.title: Pentagon Inspector General Details U.S. Losses and Challenges in Iran War

item.title: Melania Trump Encourages Children to Build ‘the Next Great Robot’ With A.I.
item.description: The first lady, who has been a champion of A.I. during her husband’s second term, said the Mountain View Elementary School students should be at the forefront of technology.

item.media:description: Melania Trump, the first lady, talking with students inside a classroom at Mountain View Elementary School, where she waded into the debate over artificial intelligence.

item.title: McCarthy Gets a Portrait Marking His Brief, Strange Speakership

item.title: Trump Defended A.I. Data Centers on Truth Social, and Commenters Clapped Back
item.description: The president’s posts about artificial intelligence on the social media platform he founded were met with an unusual volume of criticism.

item.title: Federal Employees Were Paid $9.5 Billion Not to Work in 2025 Under DOGE Effort
item.description: As part of the Department of Government Efficiency’s program to shrink the federal work force, paid administrative leave costs rose by 435 percent.
item.dc:creator: Eileen Sullivan
item.media:credit: Julia Nikhinson for The New York Times
item.media:description: The federal civilian work force has shrunk by about 12 percent since President Trump returned to office.

item.title: House Kills Bid to Impeach Trump as Democrats Split
item.description: Dozens of Democrats declined to register a position on articles of impeachment by one of their own members, Representative Al Green, that cited President Trump’s immigration crackdown.
item.dc:creator: Michael Gold
item.media:credit: Eric Lee for The New York Times
item.media:description: Representative Al Green has repeatedly defied his party’s leaders and moved to impeach President Trump, including twice last year.

item.title: ‘60 Minutes’ Season Premiere Sees Dip in Ratings
item.description: Just under 8 million people watched Sunday’s season premiere, down 21 percent from last year. Viewership for the N.F.L. lead-in fell by about the same.
item.dc:creator: Michael M. Grynbaum
item.media:description: On the season premiere of “60 Minutes,” L. Jon Wertheim interviewed Sean McVay, the coach of the Los Angeles Rams.

item.title: Steve Bannon and Bernie Sanders Condemn Tech ‘Oligarchs’ and Demand A.I. Reforms
item.description: At an event in Washington, partisanship took a back seat as elected officials, religious leaders, parents and artists called for reining in artificial intelligence.

item.media:credit: Tierney L. Cross for The New York Times
item.media:description: Senator Bernie Sanders, left, and Stephen K. Bannon spoke on Tuesday at the Pro-Human Assembly in Washington.

item.title: Senate Votes to Block Crypto Bill in Major Blow to the Industry
item.description: The landmark legislation, known as the Clarity Act, stalled in the Senate as Democrats raised concerns about President Trump’s personal investments in crypto.
item.dc:creator: David Yaffe-Bellany
item.media:description: The bill passed in the House last year, but it has faced numerous delays in the Senate.

item.title: Half of Voters Dislike Socialism Amid Progressive Wins, New Poll Finds
item.description: Zohran Mamdani, the New York City mayor and democratic socialist, was viewed more favorably than Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, a fellow high-profile member of the movement.

item.media:description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani of New York City and Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Democrat of New York, are two of the nation’s most high-profile democratic socialists.

item.title: Kash Patel Suggests FBI Agents Could Go to Election Polling Sites
item.description: Federal law prohibits armed federal officers or military personnel from being deployed to polling stations.
item.dc:creator: Devlin Barrett
item.media:credit: Kirsten Luce for The New York Times
item.media:description: U.S. law has long barred armed federal officers or military personnel from being deployed “at any place where a general or special election is held.”

item.title: A.I. Is Unpopular With Voters, a New York Times/Siena Poll Finds
item.description: As fears grow about the threat of artificial intelligence, neither party has claimed an advantage on the technology, a New York Times/Siena poll found. But voters are united in opposition to data centers.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk and Caroline Soler
item.media:description: A data center under construction last year in Abilene, Texas. The enormous computing complexes have become unpopular with voters and a significant issue in the midterms.

item.title: Supreme Court Stands Up to Trump on Mail Voting and a Few Key Issues
item.description: The justices take their time and pick their spots, but they have rejected presidential initiatives on tariffs, citizenship, the National Guard — and now the coming election.
item.dc:creator: Adam Liptak
item.media:credit: Tierney L. Cross for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration’s latest attempt to change mail-in voting rules on Monday.

item.title: Trump, the Supreme Court and the Postal Service: A History of Mail Voting
item.description: The mail system took on new prominence during the Civil War by enabling soldiers to vote from afar. On Monday, the Supreme Court blocked President Trump’s effort to give it a new role in elections.
item.dc:creator: Dan Watson
item.media:description: Two U.S. service members talked over their absentee ballots outside a bunker in Korea in 1952.

item.title: Congress Has Proposed Many Bills for A.I. Regulation. Lawmakers Have Enacted Few.
item.description: For years, Democrats and Republicans have proposed bills to address the greatest threats posed by artificial intelligence. Many remain stymied by political disputes.
item.dc:creator: Tony Romm, Dustin Volz and Michael Gold
item.media:description: Democrats and Republicans in Congress have issued a battery of measures focused on A.I., but lawmakers have largely failed to enact any of the proposals.

item.title: FEMA Could Still Lose More Jobs Despite Court Ruling
item.description: A plan to halve the agency’s sprawling work force was illegal, a judge ruled. But the court is not blocking other FEMA cuts.
item.dc:creator: Scott Dance
item.media:credit: Al Drago for The New York Times
item.media:description: The headquarters of the Federal Emergency Management Agency in Washington, D.C.

item.title: Trump Slams Supreme Court Over Mail-In Voting Ruling
item.description: In a blistering attack on the court, President Trump said “these are not the people I interviewed” to serve as justices.
item.dc:creator: Tyler Pager
item.media:description: President Trump’s attempts to change mail voting were blocked by the Supreme Court on Monday.
